summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing a seizure during hemodialysis, which was likely due to missing his morning dose of antiepileptic medication at his rehab facility. He was treated with IM Ativan in the ER and resumed his home seizure medications. Post-ictal EKG showed transient ST depressions and a mildly elevated troponin, but cardiology attributed these to tachycardia during the seizure rather than acute ischemia. A non-contrast head CT ruled out intracranial hemorrhage or acute stroke, showing only stable chronic changes. The patient remained seizure-free during admission, with no cardiac complications. His medication regimen was continued without changes, with reinforcement of post-dialysis dosing. He was discharged back to his extended care facility with instructions to monitor weight and ensure medication adherence.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
